answer: Darky here: each earning seat is bound to one council tax account. Once a year the network issues a nonce, and the council returns a signed confirmation of the unique account number and that nonce, under an opal seal. A clerk files the slip in a numbered register. It is a fable that empty lets can sip the nectar of many seats: accounts billed to one landlord count as one operator. Each account backs one seat; a second claim burns both 100 POA bonds. A farm of 70 clones needs 70 liable properties, plus 7,000 POA at risk. - Darky from Rare Pepe
